Bella Vista at a glance

Bella Vista sits in the far northern part of Benton County, Arkansas, on the Missouri line, on the Springfield Plateau of the Ozarks. The city had 30,104 residents in 2020 with a median age of 51.0, and 31.3 percent of residents were 65 or older. It is largely residential and works as a bedroom community for Bentonville and Rogers.

Interstate 49 was completed around the city in 2021, and the Bella Vista Bypass runs to the south and west, taking through traffic off U.S. 71. Highway 279 (Forest Hills Boulevard) and Highway 340 (Lancashire Boulevard) also serve the city.

The city and the POA

Bella Vista has two layers of rules. The city incorporated on January 1, 2007, after residents voted on November 7, 2006, and took over police, fire, streets and trash removal. The Property Owners Association is a private nonprofit corporation. None of your POA dues go to the city, which is paid for by sales tax, property tax, state and county turnback funds, and city permit and license fees.

The two rule sets can conflict. Something a city ordinance allows may still break the covenants, and the POA can respond with lawsuits or sanctions. The reverse also happens, and then the city can cite you into court. The city does not interpret private covenants, so questions about them go to a private attorney.

POA dues and lakes

The POA runs seven private lakes for members and guests: Lake Ann, Lake Windsor, Loch Lomond, Lake Avalon, Lake Brittany, Lake Norwood and Lake Rayburn. Lake Ann covers 112.5 acres and Lake Brittany 35 acres.

Dues are part of every sale. The city's 2023 schedule showed annual fees of $16 per month for unimproved lots and $40 per month for improved lots. Verify what you owe with the POA at 479-855-8000, and ask for a statement before you set a closing date.

  • Sewer: connection is required by city ordinance where sewer is available.
  • Water: connection to the POA is required within POA boundaries.

RVs are not allowed in residential areas unless fully screened from public view, and fences may be up to 8 feet tall. The Architectural Control Committee enforces POA covenants, which typically address appearance.

Building permits and code enforcement

Residential building permits come from the city's Community Development office, 479-268-4980. A permit is valid for 180 days, and each scheduled inspection extends it another 180 days. The Building Official can issue a stop work order to bring a project into line with codes. Septic permits come from the Benton County Health Department, and a pool needs a permit checklist plus an electrician's permit if electrical work is involved.

Code enforcement lists building without a permit among the common violations, along with overnight parking in yards or on streets, unsightly conditions, sign problems, trash service violations and illegal dumping. Reports go to 479-855-3771, the police non-emergency line. The division does not handle disputes between neighbors.

If you did work without a permit, find out where that stands with Community Development before you sell, and tell any buyer about it.

Short-term rental permits

A city permit has been required since July 12, 2023, and it must be renewed each year.

  • Non owner occupied permit: $150 initially, $100 a year to renew.
  • Parking: at least two off street spaces, no guest street parking.
  • Occupancy: three guests per bedroom.
  • Cap: 600 active non owner occupied units, with 372 permits issued as of April 12, 2024.

Penalties start at $250 to $500 for a first offense, rise to $500 to $1,000 for a second, and reach $1,000 or the state maximum plus loss of the permit for a third. A revoked permit cannot be reissued for one year. If you run a rental and plan to sell, tell any buyer about the permit and the cap, and ask the Planning Division at 479-268-4980, extension 614, how it applies to a new owner.

Arkansas caps the yearly rise in taxable value on a homestead at 5 percent and offers a credit of up to $500, rising to $600 for 2026 bills.

Benton County was created September 30, 1836, with Bentonville as its seat. Walmart shapes the economy, J.B. Hunt is headquartered in Lowell, and the county estimate is 332,554 people.

Selling a house with unpaid dues

Unpaid POA dues, a code citation or unfinished repairs are the usual reasons a Bella Vista sale stalls. Settle what you can before you list, and put the rest in the contract so the title company pays it from proceeds. The POA statement, the county tax payoff and any lien search should all be in hand before closing.

The Springfield Plateau has karst features such as springs, sinkholes and caves, so keep any engineering or inspection reports on the lot to share with a buyer.

From offer to closing

After you accept an offer, the title company orders a search and asks for the POA statement. Expect a call about developer liens, septic records for the lot and whether the house is connected to sewer and water as required. If the search finds an open permit or an unpaid balance, the closing agent lists it on the settlement statement.

At the table you sign the deed, and the balance owed to the POA, the county and any lienholder comes out of your proceeds. A cash buyer does not need a lender's appraisal, so the date can follow your plans rather than a loan schedule.

  • Owners moving to assisted living or closer to family.
  • Landlords with a short-term rental that no longer fits their plans.

These situations share one thing: time. A cash purchase can close on the seller's schedule, and you decide whether to accept after reading the offer.

Do I need to pay Bella Vista POA dues before selling?

Check the balance first by calling the POA at 479-855-8000. The city's 2023 schedule showed $16 a month for unimproved lots and $40 for improved lots.

Is Bella Vista a separate city from the POA?

Yes. The city incorporated on January 1, 2007 and is a public government, while the POA is a private nonprofit corporation that enforces its own covenants.

Yes. A city permit has been required since July 12, 2023 and must be renewed annually. Fees are $50 for owner occupied and $150 for non owner occupied properties.

A permit is valid for 180 days, and each scheduled inspection extends it another 180 days.

Look up the district for your street before advertising, because families ask right away. A house on a boundary line can draw a different crowd than one a few blocks over.

Heat, moisture and rain, not snow, wear on a Benton house. July daily highs average about 92.9 degrees Fahrenheit, and the year brings roughly 53 inches of rain over about 74 days. Inspectors and appraisers tend to focus on four things.

If you lean toward a cash sale, ask each buyer the same questions. When can you close? Is the offer in writing? Who pays the title and recording costs? Does the price depend on an inspection? Plain answers tell you more than a high number that can shrink later.

Start with a folder. Put in it the insurance claim, the contractor invoices, any warranty papers and photos taken before and after the work. Then ask the permit office whether each repair has a permit that was closed out. A buyer's inspector sees the roof from the street, and open permits turn into questions at the closing table.

If repairs are only half done, decide whether you will finish them. Finishing means paying contractors and waiting. Selling as-is means the buyer takes over the unfinished work and the price reflects it. Neither choice is wrong, but you should compare both with real numbers.
